import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    shipments = inputs["shipments"].copy()
    carrier_rates = inputs["carrier_rates"].copy()
    
    # Perform the lookup with duplicate-key resolution
    # For each row in shipments, find matching rows in carrier_rates by carrier_id
    # Then apply the first_by policy: ["effective_date DESC", "rate_id DESC"]
    
    # Merge shipments with carrier_rates on carrier_id (many-to-many at this point)
    merged = shipments.merge(
        carrier_rates,
        on="carrier_id",
        how="left"
    )
    
    # Sort by effective_date DESC, rate_id DESC globally
    # This ensures that when we group and take the first, we get the right one
    merged = merged.sort_values(
        by=["effective_date", "rate_id"],
        ascending=[False, False],
        na_position="last"
    )
    
    # Group by shipment_id and keep only the first row per shipment
    # This implements "first_by" with the sort order above
    resolved = merged.groupby("shipment_id", group_keys=False, as_index=False).first()
    
    # Fill in defaults for missed lookups
    resolved["rate_per_kg"] = resolved["rate_per_kg"].fillna(0.0)
    resolved["service_tier"] = resolved["service_tier"].fillna("NONE")
    
    # Compute freight_cost
    resolved["freight_cost"] = resolved["weight_kg"] * resolved["rate_per_kg"]
    
    # Select and order output columns
    output_columns = ["shipment_id", "carrier_id", "service_tier", "weight_kg", "rate_per_kg", "freight_cost"]
    result = resolved[output_columns].reset_index(drop=True)
    
    return {"shipment_costs": result}
